title.zh: 卷512 列傳二百九十九 土司傳一 湖广
title.en: Volume 512 Biographies 299: Native Chieftain Biographies 1: Huguang
title.raw: 卷512 列傳二百九十九 土司傳一 湖广

sentences.zh: 西南諸省，水復山重，草木蒙昧，雲霧晦冥，人生其間，叢叢虱虱，言語飲食，迥殊華風，曰苗、曰蠻，史冊屢紀，顧略有區別。

translations.literal: In the southwestern provinces, waters fold back upon one another and mountains pile layer upon layer; vegetation lies dim and obscure, clouds and mist hang dark and murky. People dwelling among them swarm thick as lice; speech and food differ utterly from Chinese custom. They are called Miao and Man, recorded repeatedly in historical annals, though with some distinction between them.
translations.idiomatic: The southwestern provinces are a country of interlaced rivers and stacked ranges, where vegetation grows rank beneath perpetual cloud and mist. The peoples who live there are countless and densely packed; their languages and diets are wholly unlike those of the Central Plains. Historians have long called them Miao or Man, yet the two categories are not quite the same.

sentences.zh: 無君長不相統屬之謂苗，各長其部割據一方之謂蠻。

translations.literal: Those without rulers or chiefs and not subordinate to one another are called Miao; those each ruling his own division and holding a region by force are called Man.
translations.idiomatic: Groups with no paramount chief and no mutual subordination are termed Miao; groups whose leaders each command a separate domain and hold territory on their own are termed Man.

sentences.zh: 若粵之僮、之黎，黔、楚之瑤，四川之倮儸、之生番，雲南之野人，皆苗之類。

translations.literal: Such as the Zhuang and Li of Guangdong, the Yao of Guizhou and Chu, the Luoluo and raw tribes of Sichuan, and the wild peoples of Yunnan—all are of the Miao type.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuang and Li of Guangdong, the Yao of Guizhou and Huguang, the Luoluo and uncivilized tribes of Sichuan, and the hill peoples of Yunnan all belong to the Miao category.

sentences.zh: 若漢書：「南夷君長以十數，夜郎最大。

translations.literal: As the Book of Han says: "Among the southern Yi there are several tens of chieftains; Yelang is the greatest."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Han records: "The southern barbarians have chieftains by the dozen; Yelang is the largest."

sentences.zh: 其西，靡莫之屬以十數，滇最大。

translations.literal: To their west, the Mo and related groups number several tens; Dian is the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: West of them, the Mo tribes and their kind likewise number in the dozens; Dian is foremost among them.

sentences.zh: 自滇以北，君長以十數，卭都最大。

translations.literal: North of Dian, chieftains again number several tens; Qiongdu is the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: North of Dian there are again chieftains by the dozen; Qiongdu ranks largest.

sentences.zh: 」在宋為羈縻州。

translations.literal: " Under the Song they became jimi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: " In Song times these became jimi prefectures—border districts left under native rule.

sentences.zh: 在元為宣慰、宣撫、招討、安撫、長官等土司。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan they became native chieftaincies such as Pacification Commissions, Comforting Commissions, Punitive Commissions, Soothing Commissions, and Chief Official offices.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan they were organized as native offices—Pacification, Comforting, Punitive, Soothing, and Chief Official commissions, among others.

sentences.zh: 湖廣之田、彭，四川之謝、向、冉，廣西之岑、韋，貴州之安、楊，雲南之刀、思，遠者自漢、唐，近亦自宋、元，各君其君，各子其子，根柢深固，族姻互結。

translations.literal: The Tian and Peng of Huguang, the Xie, Xiang, and Ran of Sichuan, the Cen and Wei of Guangxi, the An and Yang of Guizhou, the Dao and Si of Yunnan—some dating from Han and Tang, others only from Song and Yuan—each ruled his own lord, each invested his own son; roots ran deep and clans intermarried.
translations.idiomatic: The Tian and Peng clans of Huguang, the Xie, Xiang, and Ran of Sichuan, the Cen and Wei of Guangxi, the An and Yang of Guizhou, and the Dao and Si of Yunnan—some lineages reaching back to Han and Tang, others no earlier than Song and Yuan—each acknowledged only its own chief and passed succession only within its own house. Their foundations were deep and their kin networks tightly interwoven.

sentences.zh: 假我爵祿，寵之名號，乃易為統攝，故奔走惟命，皆蠻之類。

translations.literal: Granted our ranks and stipends and favored with titles, they were easily brought under control; hence they hastened at command—all belong to the Man type.
translations.idiomatic: Once the court lent them titles and salaries and honored them with official designations, they could readily be brought under centralized control, and so they hurried to obey every order. These are all of the Man type.

sentences.zh: 明代播州、藺州、水西、麓川，皆勤大軍數十萬，殫天下力而後剷平之。

translations.literal: In the Ming, Bozhou, Linzhou, Shuixi, and Luchuan each required mobilizing armies of several hundred thousand and exhausting the empire's strength before they could be uprooted.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming, Bozhou, Linzhou, Shuixi, and Luchuan each demanded armies in the hundreds of thousands and the full weight of the realm before they could finally be suppressed.

sentences.zh: 故云、貴、川、廣恆視土司為治亂。

translations.literal: Therefore Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, and Guangdong constantly regarded native chieftains as the measure of order and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Yunnan, Guizhou, Sichuan, and Guangdong always took the native chieftains as the barometer of regional stability.

sentences.zh: 清初因明制，屬平西、定南諸籓鎮撫之。

translations.literal: In the early Qing, following the Ming system, they were placed under the pacification of the Pingxi, Dingnan, and other princely fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing the court retained the Ming arrangement and left these territories under the pacification of the Pingxi, Dingnan, and other feudatory princes.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，吳三桂督雲、貴兵兩路討水西宣慰安坤之叛，平其地，設黔西、平遠、大定、威寧四府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi, Wu Sangui directed Yunnan and Guizhou troops on two routes to suppress the rebellion of An Kun, Pacification Commissioner of Shuixi; he pacified the region and established the four prefectures of Qianxi, Pingyuan, Dading, and Weining.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year 3, Wu Sangui led Yunnan and Guizhou forces along two routes against the rebellion of An Kun, the Shuixi Pacification Commissioner. After pacifying the territory, the court established the four prefectures of Qianxi, Pingyuan, Dading, and Weining.

sentences.zh: 三籓之亂，重啗土司兵為助。

translations.literal: In the Rebellion of the Three Feudatories, native chieftain troops were again enticed as auxiliaries.
translations.idiomatic: During the Rebellion of the Three Feudatories, the rebels once again recruited native chieftain forces as allies.

sentences.zh: 及叛籓戡定，餘威震於殊俗。

translations.literal: When the rebel princes were suppressed, residual awe shook the foreign peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebel princes had been crushed, the lingering prestige of the dynasty awed the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 至雍正初，而有改土歸流之議。

translations.literal: By the beginning of the Yongzheng reign, there arose discussion of replacing native rule with regular administration.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign the court began debating the policy of abolishing native chieftaincies and appointing regular officials in their place.

sentences.zh: 四年春，以鄂爾泰巡撫雲南兼總督事，奏言：「雲貴大患，無如苗蠻。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, Ortai was made Grand Coordinator of Yunnan with concurrent duties as Governor-General, and memorialized: "Of Yunnan and Guizhou's great afflictions, none surpass the Miao and Man."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of his fourth year on the throne, the emperor appointed Ortai Grand Coordinator of Yunnan with concurrent governorship and received his memorial: "The gravest trouble in Yunnan and Guizhou is none other than the Miao and Man peoples."

sentences.zh: 欲安民必先制夷，欲制夷必改土歸流。

translations.literal: To settle the people one must first control the Yi; to control the Yi one must replace native rule with regular administration.
translations.idiomatic: To secure the populace one must first subdue the frontier peoples; to subdue them one must abolish native chieftaincies and install regular officials.

sentences.zh: 而苗疆多與鄰省犬牙相錯，又必歸併事權，始可一勞永逸。

translations.literal: Yet Miao territories often interlock with neighboring provinces like dog's teeth; authority must also be consolidated before the work can be settled once for all.
translations.idiomatic: Miao territories moreover zigzag across provincial borders; only by merging administrative authority can the problem be settled once and for all.

sentences.zh: 即如東川、烏蒙、鎮雄，皆四川土府。

translations.literal: Take for example Dongchuan, Wumeng, and Zhenxiong—all native prefectures of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dongchuan, Wumeng, and Zhenxiong, for instance, were all native prefectures subordinate to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 東川與滇一嶺之隔，至滇省城四百餘里，而距四川成都千有八百里。

translations.literal: Dongchuan is separated from Yunnan by a single ridge; it is a little more than four hundred li from the Yunnan provincial capital, yet more than eighteen hundred li from Chengdu in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dongchuan lies just one mountain range from Yunnan—only four hundred-odd li from the Yunnan capital—yet more than eighteen hundred li from Chengdu in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 去冬，烏蒙土府攻掠東川，滇兵擊退，而川省令箭方至。

translations.literal: Last winter the Wumeng native prefecture raided Dongchuan; Yunnan troops repelled them, yet Sichuan's dispatch orders had only just arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Last winter the Wumeng native prefect attacked Dongchuan. Yunnan troops had already driven him off before Sichuan's orders even reached the scene.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙至滇省城亦僅六百餘里。

translations.literal: Wumeng likewise is only a little more than six hundred li from the Yunnan provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wumeng itself is only about six hundred li from the Yunnan capital.

sentences.zh: 自康熙五十三年土官祿鼎乾不法，欽差、督、撫會審畢節，以流官交質始出，益無忌憚。

translations.literal: Since the fifty-third year of Kangxi, when the native official Lu Dingqian acted lawlessly, imperial commissioners, governors, and coordinators jointly tried the case at Bijie; he emerged only after a regular official was given as hostage, and grew ever more reckless.
translations.idiomatic: Since Kangxi year 53, when the native official Lu Dingqian broke the law, imperial commissioners and provincial governors tried him jointly at Bijie. He surrendered only after a regular official was held as hostage, and thereafter grew ever bolder in his defiance.

sentences.zh: 其錢糧不過三百餘兩，而取於下者百倍。

translations.literal: Their tax grain amounted to no more than three hundred-odd taels, yet what they exacted from below was a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: Their registered tax was barely three hundred taels, yet what they collected from the people was a hundred times that amount.

sentences.zh: 一年四小派，三年一大派。

translations.literal: Four minor levies each year, one major levy every three years.
translations.idiomatic: They imposed four minor exactions every year and one major exaction every three years.

sentences.zh: 小派計錢，大派計兩。

translations.literal: Minor levies were reckoned in cash; major levies in taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Minor levies were counted in copper cash; major levies in ounces of silver.

sentences.zh: 土司一取子婦，則土民三載不敢婚。

translations.literal: When a native chieftain took a subject's bride, the native people dared not marry for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a chieftain seized a subject's bride, the people would not dare wed for three years afterward.

sentences.zh: 土民有罪被殺，其親族尚出墊刀數十金，終身無見天日之期。

translations.literal: When a native subject guilty of a crime was executed, his kin still paid several tens in gold as "cushioning the blade," and for life had no prospect of seeing daylight.
translations.idiomatic: When a guilty native was put to death, his kin still had to pay dozens of taels as "blade-padding" compensation, and his family might never again see the light of day in public life.

sentences.zh: 東川已改流三十載，仍為土目盤踞，文武長寓省城，膏腴四百里，無人敢墾。

translations.literal: Dongchuan had been under regular administration for thirty years, yet was still dominated by native headmen; civil and military officials long resided at the provincial capital, and four hundred li of fertile land—no one dared cultivate.
translations.idiomatic: Though Dongchuan had been under regular administration for thirty years, native headmen still controlled it. Civil and military officials lodged permanently at the provincial capital, and four hundred li of rich farmland lay untilled because no one dared reclaim it.

sentences.zh: 若東川、烏蒙、鎮雄改隸雲南，俾臣得相機改流，可設三府一鎮，永靖邊氛。

translations.literal: If Dongchuan, Wumeng, and Zhenxiong were transferred to Yunnan's jurisdiction so that your servant might opportunely carry out the conversion to regular rule, three prefectures and one garrison could be established to pacify the border forever.
translations.idiomatic: If Dongchuan, Wumeng, and Zhenxiong were reassigned to Yunnan so that I might replace native rule as circumstances allow, we could establish three prefectures and one garrison and secure the frontier for good.

sentences.zh: 此事連四川者也。

translations.literal: This matter concerns Sichuan as well.
translations.idiomatic: This proposal also involves Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 廣西土府州縣峒寨等司五十餘員，分隸南寧、太平、思恩、慶遠四府，多狄青征儂智高、王守仁征田州時所留設。

translations.literal: Guangxi has more than fifty native prefectures, districts, counties, dong stockades, and similar offices, distributed under the four prefectures of Nanning, Taiping, Si'en, and Qingyuan—most left from Di Qing's campaign against Nong Zhigao and Wang Shouren's campaign against Tianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi has more than fifty native prefectures, districts, stockade offices, and the like, distributed among Nanning, Taiping, Si'en, and Qingyuan—most of them remnants of Di Qing's war against Nong Zhigao and Wang Shouren's expedition against Tianzhou.

sentences.zh: 其邊患，除泗城土府外，餘皆土目，橫於土司。

translations.literal: Their border troubles, apart from the Sicheng native prefecture, all stem from native headmen who lord it over the chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Border troubles there arise, except at the Sicheng native prefecture, chiefly from native headmen who bully the recognized chieftains.

sentences.zh: 且黔、粵向以牂牁江為界，而粵之西隆州與黔之普安州逾江互相鬥入，苗寨寥闊，文武動輒推諉。

translations.literal: Moreover Guizhou and Guangdong have taken the Zangge River as their boundary, yet Guangdong's Xilong Prefecture and Guizhou's Pu'an Prefecture cross the river and encroach on each other; Miao stockades stretch vast and empty, and civil and military officials constantly pass blame.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou and Guangdong have long taken the Zangge River as their border, yet Xilong in Guangdong and Pu'an in Guizhou raid across the river into each other's territory. Miao villages lie scattered across a vast wilderness, and officials on both sides habitually shift blame to one another.

sentences.zh: 應以江北歸黔，江南歸粵，增州設營，形格勢禁。

translations.literal: The north bank should be assigned to Guizhou, the south bank to Guangdong; additional prefectures and garrisons should be established to check one another by position and force.
translations.idiomatic: The north bank should go to Guizhou and the south bank to Guangdong; new prefectures and garrisons should be added so that each side can restrain the other by geography and military presence.

sentences.zh: 此事連廣西者也。

translations.literal: This matter also concerns Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: This proposal likewise involves Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 滇邊西南界以瀾滄江，江外為車里、緬甸、老撾諸土司。

translations.literal: Yunnan's southwestern border is marked by the Lancang River; beyond the river lie the native chieftaincies of Cheli, Burma, Laos, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's southwestern frontier is defined by the Lancang River. Beyond it lie the native domains of Cheli, Burma, Laos, and others.

sentences.zh: 其江內之滇沅、威遠、元江、新平、普洱、茶山諸夷，巢穴深邃，出沒魯魁、哀牢間，無事近患腹心，有事遠通外國，自元迨明，代為邊害。

translations.literal: Within the river, the Yi of Dianyuan, Weiyuan, Yuanjiang, Xinping, Pu'er, and Chashan have lairs deep and remote, appearing and vanishing between Luokui and Ailao; when quiet they menace the heartland nearby, when active they link with foreign states afar—from Yuan through Ming they have been border scourges in every generation.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the river, the tribes of Dianyuan, Weiyuan, Yuanjiang, Xinping, Pu'er, and Chashan nest in remote fastnesses and raid between Luokui and Ailao. In peacetime they threaten the interior; in crisis they reach out to foreign powers. From Yuan through Ming they have been a perennial frontier menace.

sentences.zh: 論者謂江外宜土不宜流，江內宜流不宜土。

translations.literal: Commentators say that beyond the river native rule is fitting and regular administration is not; within the river regular administration is fitting and native rule is not.
translations.idiomatic: Policy makers have long held that beyond the river native rule is appropriate, while within it regular administration is required.

sentences.zh: 此雲南宜治之邊夷也。

translations.literal: These are the frontier Yi of Yunnan that ought to be governed.
translations.idiomatic: These are the frontier peoples of Yunnan that most need effective governance.

sentences.zh: 貴州土司向無鉗束群苗之責，苗患甚於土司。

translations.literal: Guizhou's native chieftains have never borne responsibility for restraining the Miao clans; Miao troubles exceed those of the chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou's native chieftains were never charged with controlling the Miao, and Miao unrest has proved a greater problem than the chieftains themselves.

sentences.zh: 而苗疆四周幾三千餘里，千有三百餘寨，古州踞其中，群砦環其外。

translations.literal: The Miao territory on all sides extends nearly three thousand li, with more than thirteen hundred stockades; Guzhou sits at its center, myriad fortresses ringing it without.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao region spans nearly three thousand li on every side and contains more than thirteen hundred stockades. Guzhou sits at the center, surrounded by a ring of fortified villages.

sentences.zh: 左有清江可北達楚，右有都江可南通粵，皆為頑苗蟠據，梗隔三省，遂成化外。

translations.literal: To the left the Qing River could reach north to Chu; to the right the Du River could reach south to Yue—both are coiled upon by stubborn Miao, blocking three provinces and making the region beyond transformation.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing River on the left could link north to Huguang; the Du River on the right could link south to Guangdong. Both waterways are held by obstinate Miao bands that cut off three provinces and leave the region effectively outside the empire.

sentences.zh: 如欲開江路以通黔、粵，非勒兵深入，遍加剿撫不可。

translations.literal: If one wishes to open the river route to connect Guizhou and Guangdong, troops must be compelled to penetrate deep and pacify everywhere by force and soothing—nothing less will do.
translations.idiomatic: To open the river routes between Guizhou and Guangdong, the court must send troops deep into the region and carry out thorough suppression and pacification—there is no other way.

sentences.zh: 此貴州宜治之邊夷也。

translations.literal: These are the frontier Yi of Guizhou that ought to be governed.
translations.idiomatic: These are the frontier peoples of Guizhou that most urgently require governance.

sentences.zh: 臣思前明流土之分，原因煙瘴新疆，未習風土，故因地制宜，使之鄉導彈壓。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that the Ming division between regular and native rule arose because miasma-ridden new territories were unfamiliar with local conditions; hence they adapted measures to the terrain and used natives as guides to suppress and hold down.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the Ming distinction between regular and native administration arose because the new southwestern territories were malarial and unfamiliar. The court therefore adapted policy to local conditions and relied on natives as guides and enforcers.

sentences.zh: 今歷數百載，相沿以夷治夷，遂至以盜治盜，苗、倮無追贓抵命之憂，土司無革職削地之罰，直至事大上聞，行賄詳結，上司亦不深求，以為鎮靜邊民無所控訴；

translations.literal: Now after several hundred years, the practice of using Yi to govern Yi has continued until robbers govern robbers; Miao and Luoluo have no fear of pursuing stolen goods or paying with life; native chieftains have no penalty of dismissal or land reduction—only when affairs grow grave and reach the throne do they bribe and close reports; superiors do not investigate deeply, thinking that so long as frontier people are quiet and have no petitions, all is well;
translations.idiomatic: Centuries later, the policy of letting natives govern natives has devolved into letting bandits govern bandits. Miao and Luoluo need not fear pursuit for stolen goods or capital punishment; chieftains need not fear dismissal or loss of territory. Only when a case grows too large to hide do they bribe officials to close the file. Superiors rarely probe deeply, satisfied so long as the frontier appears calm and no one petitions.

sentences.zh: 若不剷蔓塞源，縱兵刑財賦事事整飭，皆治標而非治本。

translations.literal: If the spreading vines are not cut and the source blocked, even though troops, punishments, and taxes are all put in order, it treats symptoms, not the root.
translations.idiomatic: Unless we cut away the overgrowth and stop it at the source, even perfect discipline over troops, law, and taxation will treat only symptoms, not the disease itself.

sentences.zh: 其改流之法，計擒為上，兵剿次之。

translations.literal: The method for conversion to regular rule: stratagem and capture rank first, military suppression second.
translations.idiomatic: The best method for conversion is stratagem and capture; military suppression comes second.

sentences.zh: 令其自首為上，勒獻次之。

translations.literal: Inducing voluntary surrender ranks first; compelled submission second.
translations.idiomatic: Inducing voluntary surrender is best; forced submission is second best.

sentences.zh: 惟制夷必先練兵，練兵必先選將。

translations.literal: Only in controlling the Yi must troops first be trained; in training troops generals must first be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: To control the frontier peoples one must first train troops, and to train troops one must first choose the right commanders.

sentences.zh: 誠能賞罰嚴明，將士用命，先治內，後攘外，必能所向奏效，實雲貴邊防百世之利。

translations.literal: If rewards and punishments are truly strict and clear, officers and soldiers obey orders, the interior is governed first and the exterior pacified after, success is certain wherever one turns—truly a benefit for Yunnan-Guizhou border defense for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: With strict rewards and punishments, obedient officers and men, pacification of the interior before expansion outward, every campaign will succeed. This would secure Yunnan and Guizhou's frontiers for generations to come.

sentences.zh: 」世宗知鄂爾泰才，必能辦寇，即詔以東川、烏蒙、鎮雄三土府改隸雲南。

translations.literal: " The Shizong Emperor knew Ortai's talent and that he could surely handle the bandits; he immediately decreed that the three native prefectures of Dongchuan, Wumeng, and Zhenxiong be transferred to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: " Recognizing Ortai's ability and confidence that he could handle the frontier troubles, the Yongzheng Emperor immediately ordered Dongchuan, Wumeng, and Zhenxiong transferred to Yunnan's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 六年，復鑄三省總督印，令鄂爾泰兼制廣西。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the seal of Governor-General of the three provinces was recast anew, and Ortai was ordered to control Guangxi concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year a new seal was cast for the three-province governorship, and Ortai was given concurrent authority over Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 於是自四年至九年，蠻悉改流，苗亦歸化，間有叛逆，旋即平定。

translations.literal: Thus from the fourth year to the ninth, the Man were all converted to regular rule, the Miao also submitted; occasional rebellions were promptly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: From the fourth through the ninth year of his reign, Man domains were converted to regular administration and Miao groups submitted. Occasional revolts broke out but were quickly suppressed.

sentences.zh: 其間如雍正朝古州苗疆之蕩平，乾隆朝四川大小金川之誅鋤，光緒朝西藏瞻對之征伐，皆事之钜者，分見於篇。

translations.literal: Among them, such as the sweeping pacification of the Guzhou Miao frontier in the Yongzheng reign, the extermination of Great and Little Jinchuan in Sichuan in the Qianlong reign, and the campaign against Zhandui in Tibet in the Guangxu reign—all are great affairs treated separately in their respective chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Major campaigns such as the Yongzheng pacification of the Guzhou Miao frontier, the Qianlong suppression of Great and Little Jinchuan in Sichuan, and the Guangxu expedition against Zhandui in Tibet are each recounted in their own chapters.

sentences.zh: 其土官銜號，曰宣慰司，曰宣撫司，曰招討司，曰安撫司，曰長官司。

translations.literal: Their native official titles are: Pacification Commission, Comforting Commission, Punitive Commission, Soothing Commission, and Chief Official.
translations.idiomatic: Native officials bore titles such as Pacification Commissioner, Comforting Commissioner, Punitive Commissioner, Soothing Commissioner, and Chief Official.

sentences.zh: 以勞績之多寡，分尊卑之等差，而府、州、縣之名亦往往有之。

translations.literal: According to the amount of merit, grades of high and low were distinguished; names of prefecture, department, and county also often appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Rank reflected the extent of service rendered, and many offices also bore the designations of prefecture, department, or county.

sentences.zh: 今土司之未改流者，四川宣撫使二：曰卭部，曰沙馬。

translations.literal: Among native chieftains not yet converted to regular rule today, Sichuan has two Comforting Commissioners: called Qiongdu and Shama.
translations.idiomatic: Native chieftaincies not yet converted to regular administration today include two Sichuan Comforting Commissioners: Qiongdu and Shama.

sentences.zh: 宣慰司五：曰木坪，曰明正，曰巴底，曰巴旺，曰德爾格忒。

translations.literal: Five Pacification Commissions: called Muping, Mingzheng, Badi, Bawang, and De'ergete.
translations.idiomatic: Five Pacification Commissioners: Muping, Mingzheng, Badi, Bawang, and De'ergete.

sentences.zh: 安撫使二十有一：曰長寧，曰沃日，曰瓦寺，曰梭磨，曰瓜別，曰木裏，曰革布希劄，曰巴底，曰綽斯甲布，曰喇袞，曰瓦述餘科，曰霍耳竹窩，曰霍耳章谷，曰霍耳孔撒，曰霍耳咱，曰林蔥，曰霍耳甘孜麻書，曰霍耳東科，曰春科，曰下瞻對，曰上納奪。

translations.literal: Twenty-one Soothing Commissioners: Changning, Wori, Wasi, Suomo, Guabie, Muli, Gebuxizha, Badi, Chuosijiabu, Lagun, Washuyuke, Huo'er Zhuwo, Huo'er Zhanggu, Huo'er Kongsa, Huo'er Zha, Lincong, Huo'er Ganzi Mashu, Huo'er Dongke, Chunke, Xia Zhaundui, and Shang Naduo.
translations.idiomatic: There are twenty-one Soothing Commissioners, including Changning, Wori, Wasi, Suomo, Guabie, Muli, Gebuxizha, Badi, Chuosijiabu, Lagun, Washuyuke, and the various Huo'er and Chunke offices, as well as Lower Zhaundui and Upper Naduo.

sentences.zh: 長官司二十有九：曰靜州，曰隴木，曰嶽希，曰松岡，曰卓克基，曰威龍州，曰陽地隘口，曰黨壩，曰河東，曰阿都正，曰普濟州，曰昌州，曰沈邊，曰冷邊，曰瓦述啯隴，曰瓦述毛丫，曰瓦述曲登，曰瓦述色他，曰瓦述更平，曰霍耳納林沖，曰霍耳白利，曰春科高日，曰上瞻對，曰蒙葛結，曰泥溪，曰平夷，曰蠻夷，曰沐川，曰九姓。

translations.literal: Twenty-nine Chief Officials: Jingzhou, Longmu, Yuexi, Songgang, Zhuokeji, Weilongzhou, Yangdi'aikou, Dangba, Hedong, Aduzheng, Pujizhou, Changzhou, Shenbian, Lengbian, Washu Gonglong, Washu Maoya, Washu Qudeng, Washu Seta, Washu Gengping, Huo'er Nalinchong, Huo'er Baili, Chunke Gaori, Shang Zhaundui, Menggejie, Nixi, Pingyi, Manyi, Muchuan, and Jiuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-nine Chief Officials include Jingzhou, Longmu, Yuexi, Songgang, Zhuokeji, Weilongzhou, Yangdi Pass, Dangba, Hedong, Aduzheng, Pujizhou, Changzhou, Shenbian, Lengbian, the Washu offices, the Huo'er offices, Chunke Gaori, Upper Zhaundui, Menggejie, Nixi, Pingyi, Manyi, Muchuan, and Jiuxing.

sentences.zh: 雲南宣慰使一：曰車里。

translations.literal: Yunnan has one Pacification Commissioner: called Cheli.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan has one Pacification Commissioner: Cheli.

sentences.zh: 宣撫使五：曰耿馬，曰隴川，曰幹厓，曰南甸，曰孟連。

translations.literal: Five Comforting Commissioners: Gengma, Longchuan, Ganya, Nandian, and Menglian.
translations.idiomatic: Five Comforting Commissioners: Gengma, Longchuan, Ganya, Nandian, and Menglian.

sentences.zh: 副宣撫使二：曰遮放，曰盞達。

translations.literal: Two Vice Comforting Commissioners: Zhefang and Zhanda.
translations.idiomatic: Two Vice Comforting Commissioners: Zhefang and Zhanda.

sentences.zh: 安撫使三：曰路江，曰芒市，曰猛卯。

translations.literal: Three Soothing Commissioners: Lujiang, Mangshi, and Mengmao.
translations.idiomatic: Three Soothing Commissioners: Lujiang, Mangshi, and Mengmao.

sentences.zh: 副長官司三：曰納樓，曰虧容甸，曰十二關，土府四：曰蒙化，曰景東，曰孟定，曰永寧。

translations.literal: Three Vice Chief Officials: Nalou, Kuirongdian, and Shierguan; four native prefectures: Menghua, Jingdong, Mengding, and Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: Three Vice Chief Officials—Nalou, Kuirongdian, and Shierguan—and four native prefectures: Menghua, Jingdong, Mengding, and Yongning.

sentences.zh: 土州四：曰富州，曰灣甸，曰鎮康，曰北勝。

translations.literal: Four native departments: Fuzhou, Wandian, Zhenkang, and Beisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Four native departments: Fuzhou, Wandian, Zhenkang, and Beisheng.

sentences.zh: 貴州長官司六十有二：曰中曹，曰白納，曰養龍，曰虎墜，曰程番，曰上馬，曰小程，曰盧番，曰方番，曰違番，曰羅番，曰臥龍，曰小龍，曰大龍，曰金石，曰大平，曰小平，曰大谷龍，曰小谷龍，曰木瓜，曰麻鄉，曰新添，曰平伐，曰羊場，曰慕役，曰頂營，曰沙營，曰楊義，曰都勻，曰邦水，曰思南，曰豐寧上，曰豐寧下，曰爛土，曰平定，曰樂平，曰卭水，曰偏橋，曰蠻夷，曰沿河，曰郎溪，曰都坪，曰黃道，曰都素，曰施溪，曰潭溪，曰新化，曰歐陽，曰亮寨，曰湖耳，曰中林，曰八舟，曰龍里，曰古州，曰洪州，曰省溪，曰提溪，曰烏羅，曰平頭，曰垂西，曰抵寨，曰岩門。

translations.literal: Guizhou has sixty-two Chief Officials, including Zhongcao, Bainuo, Yanglong, Huzhui, Chengfan, Shangma, Xiaocheng, Lufan, Fangfan, Weifan, Luofan, Wolong, Xiaolong, Dalong, Jinshi, Daping, Xiaoping, Dagulong, Xiaogulong, Mugua, Maxiang, Xintian, Pingfa, Yangchang, Muyi, Dingying, Shaying, Yangyi, Duyun, Bangshui, Sinan, Fengning Shang, Fengning Xia, Lantu, Pingding, Leping, Qiongshui, Pianqiao, Manyi, Yanhe, Langxi, Duping, Huangdao, Dusu, Shixi, Tanxi, Xinhua, Ouyang, Liangzhai, Hu'er, Zhonglin, Bazhou, Longli, Guzhou, Hongzhou, Shengxi, Tixi, Wuluo, Pingtou, Chuixi, Dizhai, and Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou has sixty-two Chief Officials, among them Zhongcao, Bainuo, Yanglong, Huzhui, Chengfan, the Cheng and Long offices, Jinshi, Daping, Xiaoping, the Gulong offices, Mugua, Maxiang, Xintian, Pingfa, Yangchang, Muyi, Dingying, Shaying, Yangyi, Duyun, Bangshui, Sinan, Upper and Lower Fengning, Lantu, Pingding, Leping, Qiongshui, Pianqiao, Manyi, Yanhe, Langxi, Duping, Huangdao, Dusu, Shixi, Tanxi, Xinhua, Ouyang, Liangzhai, Hu'er, Zhonglin, Bazhou, Longli, Guzhou, Hongzhou, Shengxi, Tixi, Wuluo, Pingtou, Chuixi, Dizhai, and Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 副長官司三：曰西堡，曰康莊，曰石門。

translations.literal: Three Vice Chief Officials: Xibao, Kangzhuang, and Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: Three Vice Chief Officials: Xibao, Kangzhuang, and Shimen.

sentences.zh: 廣西土州二十有六：曰忠州，曰歸德，曰果化，曰下雷，曰下石西，曰思陵，曰憑祥，曰江州，曰思州，曰萬承，曰太平，曰安平，曰龍英，曰都結，曰結安，曰上下凍，曰佶倫，曰茗州，曰茗盈，曰鎮遠，曰那地，曰南舟，曰田州，曰向武，曰都康，曰上映。

translations.literal: Guangxi has twenty-six native departments: Zhongzhou, Guide, Guohua, Xialei, Xiashixi, Siling, Pingxiang, Jiangzhou, Sizhou, Wancheng, Taiping, Anping, Longying, Dujie, Jie'an, Shangxia Dong, Jielun, Mingzhou, Mingying, Zhenyuan, Nadi, Nanzhou, Tianzhou, Xiangwu, Dukang, and Shangying.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi has twenty-six native departments, including Zhongzhou, Guide, Guohua, Xialei, Xiashixi, Siling, Pingxiang, Jiangzhou, Sizhou, Wancheng, Taiping, Anping, Longying, Dujie, Jie'an, Shangxia Dong, Jielun, Mingzhou, Mingying, Zhenyuan, Nadi, Nanzhou, Tianzhou, Xiangwu, Dukang, and Shangying.

sentences.zh: 土縣四：曰羅陽，曰上林，曰羅白，曰忻城。

translations.literal: Four native counties: Luoyang, Shanglin, Luobai, and Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Four native counties: Luoyang, Shanglin, Luobai, and Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 長官司三：曰遷隆峒，曰永定，曰永順。

translations.literal: Three Chief Officials: Qianlongdong, Yongding, and Yongshun.
translations.idiomatic: Three Chief Officials: Qianlongdong, Yongding, and Yongshun.

sentences.zh: 凡宣慰、宣撫、安撫、長官等司之承襲隸兵部，土府、土州之承襲隸吏部。

translations.literal: Succession for Pacification, Comforting, Soothing, and Chief Official commissions fell under the Ministry of War; succession for native prefectures and departments fell under the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Succession to Pacification, Comforting, Soothing, and Chief Official posts was handled by the Ministry of War; succession to native prefectures and departments by the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 凡土司貢賦，或比年一貢，或三年一貢，各因其土產，穀米、牛馬、皮、布，皆折以銀，而會計於戶部。

translations.literal: All native chieftain tribute levies were either annual or triennial, each according to local products—grain, cattle, hides, cloth—all converted to silver and accounted at the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Native chieftains paid tribute either annually or every three years, according to local products such as grain, livestock, hides, and cloth, all commuted to silver and recorded by the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 雍正七年，川陝總督岳鍾琪奏四川巴塘、里塘等處請授宣撫司三員、安撫司九員、長官司十二員，給與印結號紙，副土官四員、千戶三員、百戶二十四員，給以職銜，以分職守。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongzheng, Sichuan-Shaanxi Governor-General Yue Zhongqi memorialized that Batang, Litang, and other places in Sichuan requested three Comforting Commissioners, nine Soothing Commissioners, and twelve Chief Officials, granted seals, bonds, and tally papers; four vice native officials, three chiliarchs, and twenty-four centurions were given titles to divide duties.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 7, Governor-General Yue Zhongqi of Sichuan-Shaanxi requested appointment of three Comforting Commissioners, nine Soothing Commissioners, and twelve Chief Officials for Batang, Litang, and other Sichuan districts, with seals and credentials issued. Four vice chiefs, three chiliarchs, and twenty-four centurions received titles to divide administrative duties.

sentences.zh: 內巴塘、裏塘正副土官原無世代頭目承襲，請照流官例。

translations.literal: Among them, the principal and vice native officials of Batang and Litang originally had no hereditary headmen succession; he requested they follow the regular official precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The principal and vice chiefs of Batang and Litang had no hereditary succession; he asked that appointments follow the regular official model instead.

sentences.zh: 如有事故，開缺題補，與他土司不同。

translations.literal: If a vacancy occurred, the post would be opened and filled by memorial—differing from other native chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Vacancies would be filled by imperial appointment, unlike other hereditary chieftaincies.

sentences.zh: 湖廣之西南隅，戰國時巫郡、黔中地。

translations.literal: The southwestern corner of Huguang was in the Warring States period the territory of Wu Commandery and Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang's southwestern corner was in Warring States times the land of Wu Commandery and Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 湖北之施南、容美，湖南之永順、保靖、桑植，境地毗連，介於岳、辰、常德、宜昌之間，與川東巴、夔相接壤，南通黔，西通蜀。

translations.literal: Shinan and Rongmei in Hubei, Yongshun, Baojing, and Sangzhi in Hunan—their territories adjoin, lying between Yue, Chen, Changde, and Yichang, bordering Ba and Kui in eastern Sichuan, reaching south to Guizhou and west to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Shinan and Rongmei in Hubei and Yongshun, Baojing, and Sangzhi in Hunan form a contiguous region between Yueyang, Chenzhou, Changde, and Yichang. It borders Ba and Kui in eastern Sichuan, opens south to Guizhou, and west to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 元時所置宣慰、安撫、長官司之屬，明時因之。

translations.literal: Pacification, Soothing, and Chief Official offices established in Yuan times were continued in Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification, Soothing, and Chief Official offices established under the Yuan were retained under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 向推永、保諸宣慰，世席富強，兵亦果敢，每遇征伐，荷戈前驅，國家倚之為重。

translations.literal: Formerly the Yong and Bao Pacification Commissioners were esteemed; for generations they enjoyed wealth and strength, their troops bold and resolute; whenever campaigns arose they bore weapons in the vanguard—the state relied on them heavily.
translations.idiomatic: The Yong and Bao Pacification Commissioners were long regarded as powerful hereditary houses with bold troops who marched at the van of every campaign. The state depended on them heavily.

sentences.zh: 清有天下，僅施南、散毛、容美三宣撫使，永順、保靖兩宣慰使而已。

translations.literal: When the Qing possessed the realm, there remained only three Comforting Commissioners—Shinan, Sanmao, and Rongmei—and two Pacification Commissioners—Yongshun and Baojing.
translations.idiomatic: By the Qing conquest only three Comforting Commissioners remained—Shinan, Sanmao, and Rongmei—along with two Pacification Commissioners, Yongshun and Baojing.

sentences.zh: 雍正年間，施南、容美、永順、保靖先後納土，特設施南一府，隸北布政使，永順一府，隸南布政使。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng years, Shinan, Rongmei, Yongshun, and Baojing successively surrendered their domains; a Shinan Prefecture was specially established under the Northern Provincial Administration Commissioner, and a Yongshun Prefecture under the Southern Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongzheng reign Shinan, Rongmei, Yongshun, and Baojing surrendered in turn. The court established Shinan Prefecture under the Hubei administration and Yongshun Prefecture under the Hunan administration.

sentences.zh: 兩府既設，合境無土司名目。

translations.literal: Once the two prefectures were established, the entire region had no native chieftain designations.
translations.idiomatic: After the two prefectures were created, native chieftain titles disappeared throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 後有苗寇，分見各傳，不入此篇。

translations.literal: Later Miao bandit troubles are treated separately in other biographies and do not enter this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Later Miao rebellions are recorded in other biographies and are not included here.

sentences.zh: 施南：古巴地。

translations.literal: Shinan: ancient Ba territory.
translations.idiomatic: Shinan: the ancient territory of Ba.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢南郡蠻。

translations.literal: Qin and Han: Nan Commandery barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qin and Han it was the land of the Nan Commandery tribes.

sentences.zh: 唐施州。

translations.literal: Tang: Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang it was Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元置施南宣撫司、忠孝安撫司。

translations.literal: Yuan established the Shinan Comforting Commission and the Zhongxiao Soothing Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan established the Shinan Comforting Commission and the Zhongxiao Soothing Commission.

sentences.zh: 明玉珍時，復置忠路宣撫司。

translations.literal: In the time of Ming Yuzhen, the Zhonglu Comforting Commission was re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ming Yuzhen the Zhonglu Comforting Commission was restored.

sentences.zh: 明宣德三年，復置劍南長官司，立施州衛，領所一、宣撫司四、安撫司九、長官司十三、蠻夷官司五。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuande of the Ming, the Jiannan Chief Official Commission was re-established and Shi Guard was founded, overseeing one battalion, four Comforting Commissions, nine Soothing Commissions, thirteen Chief Officials, and five Manyi Chief offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Xuande year 3 the Jiannan Chief Official Commission was restored and Shi Guard established, governing one battalion, four Comforting Commissions, nine Soothing Commissions, thirteen Chief Officials, and five Manyi offices.

sentences.zh: 清康熙三年，施州始歸順。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi of the Qing, Shi Prefecture first submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Qing Kangxi year 3 Shi Prefecture first submitted to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 四年，改沙溪宣慰司為宣撫司，改劍南長官司為建南長官司，而施南宣撫司、忠孝安撫司、忠路安撫司如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Shaxi Pacification Commission was changed to a Comforting Commission, Jiannan Chief Official to Jiannan Chief Official of Ji'an; Shinan Comforting, Zhongxiao Soothing, and Zhonglu Soothing Commissions remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Shaxi was downgraded from Pacification to Comforting Commissioner, Jiannan Chief Official was renamed Jiannan (Ji'an) Chief Official, while Shinan Comforting, Zhongxiao Soothing, and Zhonglu Soothing Commissions remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，從湖廣總督邁柱之請，裁施州衛，設恩施縣，改歸州直隸州，原管之十五土司並隸恩施縣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, at the request of Huguang Governor-General Mai Zhu, Shi Guard was abolished and Enshi County established; Guizhou was made a directly governed department, and the fifteen native chieftaincies formerly under its jurisdiction were all placed under Enshi County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 6, at Governor-General Mai Zhu's request, Shi Guard was abolished and Enshi County created. Guizhou was made a directly governed department, and all fifteen former native chieftaincies were placed under Enshi.

sentences.zh: 十二年，忠孝安撫司田璋納土，其地入於恩施縣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Zhongxiao Soothing Commissioner Tian Zhang surrendered his domain; the land entered Enshi County.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Zhongxiao Soothing Commissioner Tian Zhang surrendered his territory, which was incorporated into Enshi County.

sentences.zh: 十三年，施南宣撫司覃禹鼎以罪改流，於是忠峒土司田光祖等並請歸流，乃以十五土司並原設恩施縣，特設施南府，領六縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Shinan Comforting Commissioner Qin Yuding was converted to regular rule for a crime; then Zhongdong native chieftain Tian Guangzu and others all requested conversion, and the fifteen chieftaincies together with the existing Enshi County were specially organized into Shinan Prefecture governing six counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Shinan Comforting Commissioner Qin Yuding was stripped of his post for misconduct and converted to regular administration. Zhongdong chieftain Tian Guangzu and others then petitioned to surrender as well. The fifteen chieftaincies and Enshi County were combined into the new Shinan Prefecture governing six counties.

sentences.zh: 容美改鶴峰州，別隸宜昌府，領於巡荊道。

translations.literal: Rongmei was changed to Hefeng Department, separately subordinate to Yichang Prefecture under the Xunjing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Rongmei became Hefeng Department, placed under Yichang Prefecture and the Xunjing surveillance circuit.

sentences.zh: 明制，施州衛，轄三里、五所、三十一土司，市郭里、都亭里、崇寧里，附郭左、右、中三所，大田軍民千戶所，支羅鎮守百戶所。

translations.literal: Under the Ming system, Shi Guard had jurisdiction over three li, five battalions, and thirty-one native chieftaincies: Shiguo Li, Duting Li, and Chongning Li; the three battalions of Left, Right, and Center attached to the garrison town; the Datian Military and Civilian Thousand-Household Battalion; and the Zhi Luo Garrison Hundred-Household Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Ming, Shi Guard governed three li districts, five battalions, and thirty-one native chieftaincies—the li of Shiguo, Duting, and Chongning; the Left, Right, and Center battalions attached to the county seat; the Datian Military-Civilian Thousand-Household Battalion; and the Zhi Luo Garrison Hundred-Household Battalion.

sentences.zh: 大田所，元為散毛峒。

translations.literal: Datian Battalion—in the Yuan it was Sanmao dong.
translations.idiomatic: The Datian Battalion had been the Sanmao dong under the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 明洪武五年定其地，二十三年屬千戶所，仍名散毛。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongwu of the Ming its territory was fixed; in the twenty-third year it was placed under a thousand-household battalion and still called Sanmao.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongwu year 5 its boundaries were fixed; in year 23 it was assigned to a thousand-household battalion and continued to be called Sanmao.

sentences.zh: 尋改為大田軍民千戶所，領百戶所一、土官百戶所十、剌惹等三峒。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter it was changed to Datian Military and Civilian Thousand-Household Battalion, overseeing one hundred-household battalion, ten native-official hundred-household battalions, and three dong including Lare.
translations.idiomatic: It was soon renamed the Datian Military-Civilian Thousand-Household Battalion, governing one hundred-household battalion, ten native-official hundred-household battalions, and three dong including Lare.

sentences.zh: 支羅所，舊隸龍潭司。

translations.literal: Zhi Luo Battalion formerly was subordinate to Longtan Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhi Luo Battalion had formerly been under Longtan Commission.

sentences.zh: 明嘉靖四十四年，因峒長黃中叛，討平之，遂割半置所立屯，以百戶二員世鎮之，而今峒司屬焉。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Jiajing of the Ming, because dong chief Huang Zhong rebelled, he was suppressed; half the territory was then cut off to establish a battalion and garrison, with two hundred-household officers hereditarily garrisoning it, and the present dong commission was placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Jiajing year 44, after dong chief Huang Zhong rebelled and was put down, half the territory was carved off to establish a garrison battalion with two hereditary hundred-household officers permanently stationed there; the remaining dong commission was placed under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 施南宣撫司，元施南道宣慰使。

translations.literal: Shinan Comforting Commission—in the Yuan, Shinan Circuit Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Shinan Comforting Commission had been the Shinan Circuit Pacification Commissioner under the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 明洪武四年，覃大富入朝，七年，升宣撫司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu of the Ming, Qin Dafu entered court; in the seventh year it was promoted to Comforting Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongwu year 4, Qin Dafu came to court; in year 7 the office was elevated to a Comforting Commission.

sentences.zh: 清因之。

translations.literal: The Qing followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing retained the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 雍正時，覃禹鼎襲。

translations.literal: In the Yongzheng period, Qin Yuding inherited.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongzheng reign, Qin Yuding succeeded to the post.

sentences.zh: 禹鼎，容美土司田明如婿也，有罪輒匿容美。

translations.literal: Yuding was the son-in-law of Rongmei native chieftain Tian Mingru; whenever guilty he would hide in Rongmei.
translations.idiomatic: Yuding was married to the daughter of Rongmei chieftain Tian Mingru, and whenever he committed an offense he would take refuge in Rongmei territory.

sentences.zh: 當事以明如之先從征紅苗有功，置勿問。

translations.literal: The authorities, because Mingru had earlier followed campaigns against the Red Miao with merit, set the matter aside and did not pursue it.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities let the matter pass unpunished because Mingru had previously earned merit in campaigns against the Red Miao.

sentences.zh: 十三年，明如被逮，自經死。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Mingru was arrested and hanged himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Mingru was apprehended and took his own life by hanging.

sentences.zh: 禹鼎以淫惡抗提，擬罪改流，以其地置利川縣。

translations.literal: Yuding, for lewdness, wickedness, and resisting arrest, was sentenced to conversion to regular rule; his territory was made Lichuan County.
translations.idiomatic: Yuding was convicted of debauchery, wickedness, and resisting arrest, stripped of his hereditary post, and his territory reorganized as Lichuan County.

sentences.zh: 東鄉安撫司，明玉珍置東鄉五路宣撫司。

translations.literal: Dongxiang Soothing Commission—in Ming Yuzhen's time the Dongxiang Five-Circuit Comforting Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Dongxiang Soothing Commission had been established by Ming Yuzhen as the Dongxiang Five-Circuit Comforting Commission.

sentences.zh: 明洪武六年改安撫司，命覃起喇為之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu of the Ming it was changed to a Soothing Commission, and Qin Qila was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongwu year 6 it was converted to a Soothing Commission with Qin Qila appointed commissioner.

sentences.zh: 清初歸附。

translations.literal: In the early Qing it submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qing it submitted to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 雍正十年，覃壽椿以長子得罪正法，改流，以其地入恩施縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongzheng, Qin Shouchun, because his eldest son offended and was lawfully executed, was converted to regular rule; his territory entered Enshi County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 10, after Qin Shouchun's eldest son was convicted and executed, the commission was abolished and its territory incorporated into Enshi County.

sentences.zh: 忠建宣撫司，明洪武四年，以田恩俊為之。

translations.literal: Zhongjian Comforting Commission—in the fourth year of Hongwu of the Ming, Tian Enjun was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongjian Comforting Commission was established in Ming Hongwu year 4 with Tian Enjun as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年，改宣撫司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year it was changed to a Comforting Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year it was reorganized as a Comforting Commission.

sentences.zh: 清初歸附。

translations.literal: In the early Qing it submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qing it submitted to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年，田興爵以橫暴不法擬流，以其地為恩施縣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng, Tian Xingjue, for tyranny and lawlessness, was sentenced to conversion to regular rule; his territory became Enshi County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 11, Tian Xingjue was convicted of tyranny and lawlessness and stripped of his post; his territory was reorganized as Enshi County.

sentences.zh: 金峒安撫司，明洪武四年，以覃耳毛為之。

translations.literal: Jindong Soothing Commission—in the fourth year of Hongwu of the Ming, Qin Ermao was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jindong Soothing Commission was founded in Ming Hongwu year 4 with Qin Ermao as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 清初歸附。

translations.literal: In the early Qing it submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qing it submitted to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 康熙四十三年，覃世英襲。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Kangxi, Qin Shiying inherited.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year 43, Qin Shiying succeeded to the post.

sentences.zh: 子邦舜，呈請改流，以其地為咸豐縣。

translations.literal: His son Bangshun petitioned for conversion to regular rule; the territory became Xianfeng County.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bangshun petitioned to surrender the domain, and the territory was reorganized as Xianfeng County.

sentences.zh: 忠峒安撫司，元置湖南鎮邊宣慰司。

translations.literal: Zhongdong Soothing Commission—in the Yuan the Hunan Frontier Pacification Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongdong Soothing Commission traced back to the Yuan-era Hunan Frontier Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 明洪武四年，命田璽玉為宣撫司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu of the Ming, Tian Xiyu was appointed Comforting Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongwu year 4, Tian Xiyu was appointed Comforting Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年，改安撫司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongle it was changed to a Soothing Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year 4 it was downgraded to a Soothing Commission.

sentences.zh: 清初田楚珍歸附，調征播州有功，仍准襲職。

translations.literal: In the early Qing Tian Chuzhen submitted; for merit in the mobilized campaign against Bozhou, he was still permitted to inherit the post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing, Tian Chuzhen submitted. For his service in the campaign against Bozhou he was allowed to retain the hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 雍正十二年，田光祖糾十五土司呈請納土歸流，以其地入宣恩縣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yongzheng, Tian Guangzu joined with fifteen native chieftains in petitioning to surrender territory and convert to regular rule; the land entered Xuan'en County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 12, Tian Guangzu organized fifteen chieftains to petition for territorial surrender and regular administration; their lands were incorporated into Xuan'en County.

sentences.zh: 散毛宣撫司，元為散毛府。

translations.literal: Sanmao Comforting Commission—in the Yuan it was Sanmao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Sanmao Comforting Commission had been Sanmao Prefecture under the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 至正六年，改宣撫司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhizheng it was changed to a Comforting Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng year 6 it was converted to a Comforting Commission.

sentences.zh: 明洪武四年，命覃野旺為宣撫司，割其半為大田所。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu of the Ming, Qin Yewang was appointed Comforting Commissioner; half the territory was cut off to form Datian Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongwu year 4, Qin Yewang was appointed commissioner; half the domain was carved off to establish the Datian Battalion.

sentences.zh: 清初覃勳麟歸附，仍准襲職。

translations.literal: In the early Qing Qin Xunlin submitted and was still permitted to inherit the post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing, Qin Xunlin submitted and was allowed to retain the hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，覃烜納土，以其地入來鳳縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, Qin Xuan surrendered his territory; the land entered Laifeng County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 13, Qin Xuan surrendered his domain, which was incorporated into Laifeng County.

sentences.zh: 忠路安撫司，明洪武四年，命覃英為安撫司。

translations.literal: Zhonglu Soothing Commission—in the fourth year of Hongwu of the Ming, Qin Ying was appointed Soothing Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhonglu Soothing Commission was established in Ming Hongwu year 4 with Qin Ying as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 清康熙元年，覃承國歸附，以征譚逆功襲前職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi of the Qing, Qin Chengguo submitted; for merit in the campaign against Tan the rebel he inherited his former post.
translations.idiomatic: In Qing Kangxi year 1, Qin Chengguo submitted and, for his service suppressing Tan's rebellion, was confirmed in his hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，覃楚梓納土，以其地改利川縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, Qin Chuzi surrendered his territory; the land was changed to Lichuan County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 13, Qin Chuzi surrendered his domain, which was reorganized as Lichuan County.

sentences.zh: 忠孝安撫司，元至正十一年，改軍民府。

translations.literal: Zhongxiao Soothing Commission—in the eleventh year of Zhizheng of the Yuan it was changed to a Military and Civilian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongxiao Soothing Commission had been reorganized as a Military-Civilian Prefecture in Yuan Zhizheng year 11.

sentences.zh: 明洪武四年，以田墨施為安撫司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu of the Ming, Tian Moshi was appointed Soothing Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongwu year 4, Tian Moshi was appointed Soothing Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 清因之。

translations.literal: The Qing followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing retained the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，田京襲，累授總兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi, Tian Jing inherited; he was repeatedly appointed regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year 8, Tian Jing succeeded to the post and was later promoted to regional commander.

sentences.zh: 十九年，告休。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，田璋納土，以其地為恩施縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, Tian Zhang surrendered his territory; the land became Enshi County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 13, Tian Zhang surrendered his domain, which was reorganized as Enshi County.

sentences.zh: 高羅安撫司，元高羅寨長官司。

translations.literal: Gaoluo Soothing Commission—in the Yuan, Gaoluo Stockade Chief Official.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoluo Soothing Commission had been the Gaoluo Stockade Chief Official under the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 明洪武六年，改安撫司，以田大名為之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongwu of the Ming it was changed to a Soothing Commission; Tian Daming was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongwu year 6 it was elevated to a Soothing Commission with Tian Daming as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 清順治初，田飛龍歸附，仍准世襲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi of the Qing, Tian Feilong submitted and was still permitted hereditary inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shunzhi reign, Tian Feilong submitted and was confirmed in the hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，田昭納土，以其地入宣恩縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, Tian Zhao surrendered his territory; the land entered Xuan'en County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 13, Tian Zhao surrendered his domain, which was incorporated into Xuan'en County.

sentences.zh: 木冊長官司，元置安撫司。

translations.literal: Muce Chief Official—in the Yuan a Soothing Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Muce Chief Official traced back to a Yuan-era Soothing Commission.

sentences.zh: 明永樂六年，改長官司，以田穀佐為長官司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongle of the Ming it was changed to a Chief Official Commission; Tian Guzuo was appointed chief official.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Yongle year 6 it was downgraded to a Chief Official Commission with Tian Guzuo as chief.

sentences.zh: 清初，田經國歸附，仍與世襲。

translations.literal: In the early Qing, Tian Jingguo submitted and was still granted hereditary inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing, Tian Jingguo submitted and retained the hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，田應鼎納土，以其地入宣恩縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, Tian Yingding surrendered his territory; the land entered Xuan'en County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 13, Tian Yingding surrendered his domain, which was incorporated into Xuan'en County.

sentences.zh: 大旺安撫司，元至正置。

translations.literal: Dawang Soothing Commission—established in the Yuan Zhizheng period.
translations.idiomatic: The Dawang Soothing Commission was established in the late Yuan.

sentences.zh: 明洪武四年，以田驢蹄為安撫司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu of the Ming, Tian Lüti was appointed Soothing Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongwu year 4, Tian Lüti was appointed Soothing Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 清康熙初，田永封歸附，仍准襲職。

translations.literal: In the early Kangxi of the Qing, Tian Yongfeng submitted and was still permitted to inherit the post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kangxi reign, Tian Yongfeng submitted and was allowed to retain the hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，田正元納土，以其地入來鳳縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, Tian Zhengyuan surrendered his territory; the land entered Laifeng County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 13, Tian Zhengyuan surrendered his domain, which was incorporated into Laifeng County.

sentences.zh: 臨壁長官司，原附大旺。

translations.literal: Linbi Chief Official—originally attached to Dawang.
translations.idiomatic: The Linbi Chief Official had originally been subordinate to Dawang.

sentences.zh: 清康熙元年，頒給田琦印信，仍與世襲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi of the Qing, the seal and credentials were issued to Tian Qi; hereditary inheritance was still granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Qing Kangxi year 1, Tian Qi was issued his seal of office and confirmed in the hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，田封疆納土，以其地入來鳳縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, Tian Fengjiang surrendered his territory; the land entered Laifeng County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 13, Tian Fengjiang surrendered his domain, which was incorporated into Laifeng County.

sentences.zh: 東流安撫司，原附大旺。

translations.literal: Dongliu Soothing Commission—originally attached to Dawang.
translations.idiomatic: The Dongliu Soothing Commission had originally been subordinate to Dawang.

sentences.zh: 唐崖長官司，元置千戶所。

translations.literal: Tangya Chief Official—in the Yuan a thousand-household battalion was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Tangya Chief Official traced back to a Yuan-era thousand-household battalion.

sentences.zh: 明洪武七年，改長官司。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Hongwu of the Ming it was changed to a Chief Official Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongwu year 7 it was converted to a Chief Official Commission.

sentences.zh: 清初覃宗禹歸附，仍與世襲。

translations.literal: In the early Qing Qin Zongyu submitted and was still granted hereditary inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing, Qin Zongyu submitted and retained the hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，覃梓桂納土，以其地入咸豐縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, Qin Zigui surrendered his territory; the land entered Xianfeng County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 13, Qin Zigui surrendered his domain, which was incorporated into Xianfeng County.

sentences.zh: 龍潭安撫司，明洪武四年，以田應虎為安撫司。

translations.literal: Longtan Soothing Commission—in the fourth year of Hongwu of the Ming, Tian Yinghu was appointed Soothing Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Longtan Soothing Commission was established in Ming Hongwu year 4 with Tian Yinghu as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 清初歸附，仍准世襲。

translations.literal: In the early Qing it submitted and was still permitted hereditary inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qing it submitted to the dynasty and was confirmed in the hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，田貴龍納土，以其地入咸豐縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, Tian Guilong surrendered his territory; the land entered Xianfeng County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 13, Tian Guilong surrendered his domain, which was incorporated into Xianfeng County.

sentences.zh: 沙溪安撫司，明置。

translations.literal: Shaxi Soothing Commission—established in the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Shaxi Soothing Commission was established under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 清初歸附。

translations.literal: In the early Qing it submitted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qing it submitted to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，黃天奇襲安撫司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi, Huang Tianqi inherited the Soothing Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year 4, Huang Tianqi succeeded as Soothing Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天奇子楚昌。

translations.literal: Tianqi's son was Chuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi's son was named Chuchang.

sentences.zh: 初，楚昌入施州衛學為諸生。

translations.literal: At first, Chuchang entered Shi Guard school as a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Chuchang enrolled as a student at the Shi Guard Confucian school.

sentences.zh: 時諸司爭並，民鮮知禮，楚昌折節力學，有時名。

translations.literal: At that time the various commissions competed for annexation; the people scarcely knew ritual. Chuchang restrained himself and strove in study, gaining reputation in his time.
translations.idiomatic: As the various chieftaincies vied for territory and the people had little knowledge of propriety, Chuchang applied himself rigorously to his studies and won renown.

sentences.zh: 及襲職，設官學，公餘與多士講肄，多所成就。

translations.literal: When he inherited the post, he established an official school; in spare time from public duties he lectured and studied with many scholars, and many were nurtured to achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Upon succeeding to the post he founded an official school and, in hours away from administration, lectured with local scholars and nurtured many talents.

sentences.zh: 楚昌死，子正爵襲。

translations.literal: When Chuchang died, his son Zhengjue inherited.
translations.idiomatic: After Chuchang died, his son Zhengjue succeeded to the office.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，改流，其地入於利川縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, it was converted to regular rule; the territory entered Lichuan County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 13 the commission was abolished and its territory incorporated into Lichuan County.

sentences.zh: 卯峒長官司，清雍正十三年，長官司向舜納土，以其地入來鳳縣。

translations.literal: Maodong Chief Official—in the thirteenth year of Yongzheng of the Qing, Chief Official Xiang Shun surrendered his territory; the land entered Laifeng County.
translations.idiomatic: The Maodong Chief Official: in Qing Yongzheng year 13, Chief Xiang Shun surrendered his domain, which was incorporated into Laifeng County.

sentences.zh: 漫水宣撫司，清初，宣撫司向國泰歸附，仍准世襲。

translations.literal: Manshui Comforting Commission—in the early Qing, Comforting Commissioner Xiang Guotai submitted and was still permitted hereditary inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: The Manshui Comforting Commission: early in the Qing, Commissioner Xiang Guotai submitted and was confirmed in the hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 雍正十三年，向庭官納土，其地入於來鳳縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, Xiang Tingguan surrendered his territory; the land entered Laifeng County.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 13, Xiang Tingguan surrendered his domain, which was incorporated into Laifeng County.

sentences.zh: 西萍長官司，雍正十三年裁，其地入於咸豐縣。

translations.literal: Xiping Chief Official—in the thirteenth year of Yongzheng it was abolished; the land entered Xianfeng County.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiping Chief Official was abolished in Yongzheng year 13, and its territory was incorporated into Xianfeng County.

sentences.zh: 建南長官司，明宣德五年置。

translations.literal: Jiannan Chief Official—established in the fifth year of Xuande of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiannan Chief Official was established in Ming Xuande year 5.

sentences.zh: 清雍正十三年裁，其地入於利川縣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng of the Qing it was abolished; the land entered Lichuan County.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished in Qing Yongzheng year 13, and its territory was incorporated into Lichuan County.

sentences.zh: 容美土司，唐元和元年，田行皋從高崇文討平劉辟，授施溱溶萬招討把截使，仍知四州事。

translations.literal: Rongmei native chieftain—in the first year of Yuanhe of the Tang, Tian Xinggao followed Gao Chongwen in suppressing Liu Pi; he was appointed punitive-reconnaissance interception commissioner of Shi, Qin, Rong, and Wan, and still administered the affairs of the four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The Rongmei chieftaincy: in Tang Yuanhe year 1, Tian Xinggao joined Gao Chongwen's campaign to suppress Liu Pi and was appointed punitive commissioner over Shi, Qin, Rong, and Wan, while continuing to govern four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 宋有田思政。

translations.literal: In the Song there was Tian Zhengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song the line was held by Tian Zhengzhi.

sentences.zh: 元有田乾亨。

translations.literal: In the Yuan there was Tian Qianheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it passed to Tian Qianheng.

sentences.zh: 明洪武三年，田光寶以元所授誥敕詣行在請換，乃命光寶仍為宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu of the Ming, Tian Guangbao brought the patent of appointment granted by the Yuan to the temporary imperial residence to request exchange; Guangbao was then ordered to remain Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Ming Hongwu year 3, Tian Guangbao traveled to the imperial camp with his Yuan-era patent to request reconfirmation; the court appointed him Pacification Commissioner anew.

sentences.zh: 傳至田既霖，清順治間歸附，仍授宣慰使。

translations.literal: The succession reached Tian Jilin; in the Shunzhi period of the Qing he submitted and was still appointed Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The line descended to Tian Jilin, who submitted during the Shunzhi reign and was confirmed as Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 子甘霖襲。

translations.literal: His son Ganlin inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ganlin succeeded to the post.

sentences.zh: 甘霖字特雲，著合浦集。

translations.literal: Ganlin, styled Tieyun, authored the Hepu ji.
translations.idiomatic: Ganlin, courtesy name Tieyun, wrote the Hepu ji collection.

sentences.zh: 甘霖子舜年，字九峰，受吳逆偽承恩伯敕，後繳。

translations.literal: Ganlin's son Shunian, styled Jiufeng, received a fake patent from the Wu rebel as Earl who receives grace; he later surrendered it.
translations.idiomatic: Ganlin's son Shunian, courtesy name Jiufeng, had once accepted a spurious patent from the Wu pretender making him "Earl Who Receives Grace"; he later turned it in to the authorities.

sentences.zh: 奉檄從征有勞績，頗招名流習文史，刻有廿一史纂。

translations.literal: Ordered by edict to follow campaigns, he had meritorious achievement; he fairly recruited noted figures to study literature and history, and carved block-printed the Compendium of the Twenty-One Histories.
translations.idiomatic: Called to military service by imperial order, he earned distinction in the field. He also gathered literary men to study the classics and history, and published a printed compendium of the Twenty-One Histories.

sentences.zh: 日自課，某日讀某經、閱某史至某處，刻於書之空處，用小印志之。

translations.literal: Each day he set himself lessons; on such-and-such a day he read such-and-such a classic or perused such-and-such a history to such-and-such a point—all carved in empty spaces in the books and marked with a small seal.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a daily reading schedule, noting in the margins of his books which classic he had read or which history he had studied and how far he had progressed, stamping each entry with a small personal seal.

sentences.zh: 有白鹿堂集、容陽世述錄。

translations.literal: He had the Bailutang ji and Rongyang shishu lu.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Bailutang ji and the Rongyang shishu lu.

sentences.zh: 子明如襲職。

translations.literal: His son Mingru inherited the post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mingru succeeded to the office.

sentences.zh: 以放肆為趙申喬劾奏，奉旨原宥。

translations.literal: For license he was impeached and memorialized by Zhao Shenqiao; an imperial decree pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shenqiao impeached him for misconduct, but the throne issued an edict granting him pardon.

sentences.zh: 雍正十一年，再為邁柱嚴參，明如移駐平山寨儗抗拒，為石樑長官司張彤砫催迫，明如自盡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongzheng, he was again severely memorialized against by Mai Zhu; Mingru moved his encampment to Pingshan Stockade intending to resist; pressed by Zhang Tong of Shiliang Chief Official Commission who was stationed there, Mingru killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng year 11, Governor Mai Zhu submitted another stern denunciation. Mingru shifted his headquarters to Pingshan Stockade as if preparing to resist, but when Zhang Tong, chief of Shiliang, stationed there and pressed him to comply, Mingru took his own life.

sentences.zh: 改土歸流，改司為鶴峰州，隸宜昌府。

translations.literal: Converting native territory to regular rule, the commission was changed to Hefeng Prefecture, subordinate to Yichang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The domain was converted to regular administration: the commission became Hefeng Prefecture under Yichang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 永順：漢武陵，隋辰州，唐溪州地。

translations.literal: Yongshun: Han Wuling, Sui Chenzhou, Tang Xizhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshun: in Han times it was Wuling; under the Sui it belonged to Chenzhou; under the Tang it was Xizhou territory.

sentences.zh: 宋時為永順州。

translations.literal: In Song times it was Yongshun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song it was Yongshun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元時，彭萬潛自改為永順等處軍民安撫司。

translations.literal: In Yuan times, Peng Wanqian on his own changed it to the Yongshun and other regions Military-Civilian Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuan dynasty, Peng Wanqian reorganized the territory as the Military and Civil Pacification Commission of Yongshun and adjacent areas.

sentences.zh: 明洪武五年，改宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Ming Hongwu, it was changed to Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Hongwu reign (1372), the office was reclassified as Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 清順治四年，恭順王孔有德至辰州，宣慰使彭宏澎率三知州、六長官、三百八十峒苗蠻歸附。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qing Shunzhi, Prince Gongshun Kong Youde arrived at Chenzhou; Pacification Commissioner Peng Hongpeng led three native prefects, six native chiefs, and three hundred eighty dong Miao and Man tribes to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Shunzhi reign (1647), Prince Gongshun Kong Youde reached Chenzhou, and Pacification Commissioner Peng Hongpeng brought three native prefects, six native chiefs, and three hundred eighty Miao and Man communities in submission.

sentences.zh: 十四年，頒給宣慰使印，並設流官經歷一員。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the Pacification Commissioner seal was issued, and one regular official director was also established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (1657), the court issued the Pacification Commissioner's seal and appointed one regular administrative director.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，吳三桂叛踞辰龍關，授永順宣慰使彭廷椿偽印，廷椿繳之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi, Wu Sangui rebelled and occupied Chenlong Pass, conferring a false seal upon Yongshun Pacification Commissioner Peng Tingchun; Tingchun surrendered it.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Kangxi reign (1671), Wu Sangui rebelled and seized Chenlong Pass, granting a counterfeit seal to Yongshun Pacification Commissioner Peng Tingchun, who promptly returned it to the court.

sentences.zh: 奉旨賞其子宏海總兵銜，令率土兵協剿，有功，授宣慰司印。

translations.literal: By imperial order his son Honghai was rewarded with the rank of regional commander, ordered to lead native troops in joint suppression; for merit, the Pacification Commission seal was granted.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial decree, his son Honghai was given the rank of regional commander and ordered to lead native troops in the joint campaign. For his service, he received the Pacification Commission seal.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，宣慰使彭肇槐納土，請歸江西祖籍，有旨嘉獎，授參將，並世襲拖沙喇哈番之職，賜銀一萬兩，聽其在江西祖籍立產安插，改永順司為府，附郭為永順縣，分永順白崖峒地為龍山縣。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, Pacification Commissioner Peng Zhaohuai surrendered the land, requesting return to his Jiangxi ancestral home; there was an edict of commendation, appointing him brigade vice-commander and hereditary Tuosha Lahafan, bestowing ten thousand taels of silver, permitting him to establish property and settle in his Jiangxi ancestral home, changing Yongshun Commission to a prefecture, the attached seat becoming Yongshun County, dividing Yongshun Baiya Dong territory into Longshan County.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Yongzheng reign (1728), Pacification Commissioner Peng Zhaohuai surrendered his territory and asked to return to his ancestral home in Jiangxi. The emperor commended him, appointed him brigade vice-commander with a hereditary Tuosha Lahafan rank, granted ten thousand taels of silver, and allowed him to establish an estate and settle in Jiangxi. Yongshun Commission was converted into a prefecture; the seat became Yongshun County, and land from Yongshun's Baiya Dong was carved off to form Longshan County.

sentences.zh: 南渭州土知州，屬永順司。

translations.literal: Nanwei Prefecture native prefect, subordinate to Yongshun Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The native prefect of Nanwei Prefecture was under the Yongshun Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 元至元中，置安撫司。

translations.literal: In the middle of Yuan Zhiyuan, a Pacification Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the middle of the Zhiyuan period, a pacification commission was established there.

sentences.zh: 明洪武二年，以彭萬金為土知州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Ming Hongwu, Peng Wanjin was made native prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Hongwu reign (1369), Peng Wanjin was appointed native prefect.

sentences.zh: 傳至彭應麟，清順治四年，歸附。

translations.literal: Transmitted to Peng Yinglin; in the fourth year of Qing Shunzhi, he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed to Peng Yinglin, who submitted in the fourth year of the Shunzhi reign (1647).

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，彭宗國納土，以其地入永順縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, Peng Zongguo surrendered the land, its territory incorporated into Yongshun County.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign (1727), Peng Zongguo surrendered his territory, which was incorporated into Yongshun County.

sentences.zh: 施溶州土知州，在永順司東南。

translations.literal: Shirong Prefecture native prefect, southeast of Yongshun Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The native prefect of Shirong Prefecture lay southeast of the Yongshun Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 元會溪、施溶等處長官司。

translations.literal: Yuan Huixi, Shirong and other places native chief office.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan, it was the native chief office of Huixi, Shirong, and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 明洪武二年，改州，以田建霸為土知州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Ming Hongwu, it was changed to a prefecture, with Tian Jianba as native prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Hongwu reign (1369), the office was elevated to a prefecture, with Tian Jianba appointed native prefect.

sentences.zh: 傳至田茂年，清順治四年，歸附。

translations.literal: Transmitted to Tian Maonian; in the fourth year of Qing Shunzhi, he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed to Tian Maonian, who submitted in the fourth year of the Shunzhi reign (1647).

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，田永豐納土。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, Tian Yongfeng surrendered the land.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign (1727), Tian Yongfeng surrendered his territory.

sentences.zh: 上溪州土知州，屬永順司。

translations.literal: Shangxi Prefecture native prefect, subordinate to Yongshun Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The native prefect of Shangxi Prefecture was under the Yongshun Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 明洪武二年，以張義保為土知州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Ming Hongwu, Zhang Yibao was made native prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Hongwu reign (1369), Zhang Yibao was appointed native prefect.

sentences.zh: 傳至張漢卿，清順治四年，歸附。

translations.literal: Transmitted to Zhang Hanqing; in the fourth year of Qing Shunzhi, he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed to Zhang Hanqing, who submitted in the fourth year of the Shunzhi reign (1647).

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，張漢儒納土。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, Zhang Hanru surrendered the land.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign (1727), Zhang Hanru surrendered his territory.

sentences.zh: 臘惹峒長官司，元屬思州，以向孛爍為總管。

translations.literal: Lara Dong native chief office; in Yuan subordinate to Sizhou, with Xiang Boshuo as superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: The Lara Dong native chief office had belonged to Sizhou under the Yuan, with Xiang Boshuo as superintendent.

sentences.zh: 明洪武五年，改屬永順司，以田世貴為長官司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Ming Hongwu, jurisdiction changed to Yongshun Commission, with Tian Shigui as native chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Hongwu reign (1372), it was transferred to Yongshun's jurisdiction, with Tian Shigui appointed native chief.

sentences.zh: 傳至田仕朝，清順治四年，歸附。

translations.literal: Transmitted to Tian Shichao; in the fourth year of Qing Shunzhi, he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The line passed to Tian Shichao, who submitted in the fourth year of the Shunzhi reign (1647).

sentences.zh: 雍正五年，田中和納土。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, Tian Zhonghe surrendered the land.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Yongzheng reign (1727), Tian Zhonghe surrendered his territory.

sentences.zh: 麥著黃峒長官司，元曰麥著土村，屬思州。

translations.literal: Maizhu Huang Dong native chief office; in Yuan called Maizhu native village, subordinate to Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Maizhu Huang Dong native chief office was known under the Yuan as the Maizhu native village and fell under Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 明洪武五年，改屬永順司，以黃穀踵為長官司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Ming Hongwu, jurisdiction changed to Yongshun Commission, with Huang Guzhong as native chief.
